summary: Connect spike-based computation to practical neural-data workloads with explicit hardware and evaluation boundaries.
outcomes: Map an event-driven signal-processing task to a neuromorphic software model.
Compare latency, accuracy and energy measurements fairly with conventional compute.
sequence: Separate biological spikes, encoded events and artificial neurons
Compare floating-point simulation and hardware constraints
Measure end-to-end costs including encoding and I/O

visual.question: Where does event sparsity save work, and where does overhead dominate?
visual.interaction: Change input activity and routing density in an explicitly simulated cost model.

practice.task: Prototype a small event-filtering task using a supported simulator.
practice.success: Reports functionality and distinguishes simulated operation counts from measured hardware energy.
